page: Vultr vhp-4c-12gb-intel is a High Performance family virtual server configured with 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon cores using hyper-threading. The instance features an x86_64 architecture, a 2.0 GHz clock speed, and a cache hierarchy consisting of 32 KB L1d, 4 MB L2, and 16 MB L3 cache. It includes 12.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.0 GB per core, and is bundled with 260 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. One complimentary public IPv4 address is included.

Benchmark data reveals a mixture of average and weak performance characteristics, typical of shared CPU allocations. Single-core stress-ng performance is average at 1466.08, but multi-core performance drops to the weak category at 5747.52. Memory bandwidth shows a similar pattern, with cached small-block reads performing at an average of 421.33 GB/sec, while uncached large-block reads are weak at 36.96 GB/sec. Cryptographic and database benchmarks, such as Passmark database operations (1351.82) and Passmark CPU encryption (2184.22), fall into the weak category. However, the server maintains average performance in Redis SET operations, achieving 6.4 million operations per second, and single-threaded gzip compression at 24.18 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of this instance is its shared CPU allocation, which limits multi-threaded scaling and leads to poor multi-threaded bzip3 decompression performance. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers a high-capacity 260 GB NVMe SSD and a moderate 12.0 GB memory footprint at a lower tier, making it resource-dense for storage-heavy but compute-light workloads. It is best suited for general-purpose applications, lightweight web serving, Redis caching, and development environments that do not require sustained, dedicated multi-core CPU performance.
